name: Under Armour, Inc.
event_type: First public disclosure: SEC and DOJ investigation of accounting practices
note: 8-K confirming an SEC and DOJ investigation of certain accounting practices, after a Wall Street Journal article on November 3, 2019; the company had been responding to requests since July 2017. Later SEC action, release 2021-78 (May 3, 2021; https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2021-78): for six consecutive quarters beginning Q3 2015, pulled forward $408 million of existing orders without disclosing the impact. $9 million penalty, settled without admitting or denying the findings.

name: Kraft Heinz Co
event_type: First public disclosure: SEC subpoena on procurement accounting
note: Q4 2018 results release disclosed an October 2018 SEC subpoena tied to an investigation of the procurement area, and a $25 million out-of-period increase to cost of products sold. Restated in June 2019. Later SEC action, release 2021-174 (September 3, 2021; https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2021-174): expense management misconduct from Q4 2015 through 2018; the restatement corrected $208 million of improperly recognized cost savings. $62 million penalty.

name: GENERAL ELECTRIC CO
event_type: First public disclosure: insurance reserve shortfall
note: 8-K reporting an $8.9 billion increase in run-off insurance policy benefit reserves (a $6.2 billion after-tax charge in Q4 2017). It covers the insurance issue only. Later SEC action, release 2020-312 (December 9, 2020; https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2020-312): misleading disclosures about GE Power profits (2016 to Q3 2017) and insurance claim cost estimates (2015 to 2017). $200 million penalty.

name: Super Micro Computer, Inc.
event_type: First public disclosure: Audit Committee investigation of revenue recognition
note: Preliminary Q1 FY2018 results release disclosed an Audit Committee investigation of a sale first recorded as revenue in the quarter ended December 31, 2016, and of any similar transactions, and that the FY2017 10-K was delayed. (A late-filing notice on August 29, 2017 gave no reason.) Earliest disclosure of the investigation found. Later SEC action, release 2020-190 (August 25, 2020; https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2020-190): premature revenue recognition and understated expenses over at least three years. $17.5 million penalty.

name: MIMEDX GROUP, INC.
event_type: First public disclosure: Audit Committee investigation and delayed 10-K
note: Release postponing FY2017 results and the 10-K pending an Audit Committee investigation of allegations about certain sales and distribution practices. Later SEC action, release 2019-243 (November 26, 2019; https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2019-243): alleged premature revenue recognition on sales to distributors from 2013 to 2017, exaggerating revenue growth. $1.5 million company penalty.

name: SYNCHRONOSS TECHNOLOGIES INC
event_type: First public disclosure: review of prior-period accounting and delayed 10-Q
note: Release delaying the Q1 2017 10-Q while management and the Audit Committee reviewed the accounting of certain transactions in prior periods. An 8-K reporting June 8, 2017 said FY2015 and FY2016 financial statements should no longer be relied on. Later SEC action, release 2022-101 (June 7, 2022; https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2022-101): accounting misconduct from 2013 to 2017; the July 2018 restatement covered about $190 million of revenue. $12.5 million penalty.

name: HERTZ CORP
event_type: First public disclosure: non-reliance on 2011 financial statements
note: 8-K filed by Hertz Global Holdings and The Hertz Corporation: 2011 financial statements should no longer be relied on, and 2012 and 2013 needed correcting (errors included non-fleet asset depreciation timing and receivable allowances). Later SEC order entered December 31, 2018 (File 3-18965; https://www.sec.gov/enforcement-litigation/administrative-proceedings/33-10601-s): filings from February 2012 through March 2014 misstated pre-tax income; the July 2015 restatement removed $235 million. $16 million penalty.
